chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Safwan, from Al-Jahm ibn Humayd, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Relatives may be for me who are not upon my command (Wilayah). Do they have a right upon me?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, the right of kinship. Nothing cuts it off. And if they are upon your command, they have two rights: the right of kinship and the right of Islam.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the rights of relatives who are upon the Imam's command versus those who are not?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the perpetual bond of kinship (Haq al-Rahim) and the additional spiritual merit of shared faith (Haq al-Islam). This distinction highlights that while familial ties remain obligatory regardless of religious alignment, the reward for maintaining them with those who share the Imam's authority is multiplied by the dual virtue of blood relation and Islamic brotherhood. This underscores the Shia emphasis on preserving family bonds even with non-Muslim or less devout relatives, while prioritizing those within the religious community.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Salih Bin Abu Hammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Safwan, from Al Jaham Bin Humeyd who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘There happen to be relatives for him being upon other than my matter (Al-Wilayah). Is there (any) right for them upon me?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, the right of kinship. Nothing can cut if off. And had they been upon your matter (Al-Wilayah), there would have been two rights for them – the right of the kinship and the right of Al-Islam’.
en.sarwar: 30. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Salih ibn abu Hammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Safwan from al-Jahm ibn Hamid who has said the following:

“I asked abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) ‘I have certain relatives who are not in my way (my belief). Do they have any rights on me?’ The Imam said, ‘Yes, it is the right of maintaining good relations with relatives that is not cut off by any means. Had they been in the same way as your way they would have had two rights: The right of relatives and the right because of Islam.’”
